title: Japanese Imperial Era Calendar
intro: Japan's modern imperial era system labels years according to official reign-era boundaries while retaining Gregorian months and days.
summary: A date includes an era name, its year number, month and day.
origin: The Gregorian calendar was adopted for Japanese civil use in 1873; the provider covers the modern Meiji, Taisho, Showa, Heisei and Reiwa eras.
structure: The era year is Gregorian year minus the era's starting year plus one. The first year begins at the actual era transition, not necessarily on 1 January.
pattern_note: The first year is called gannen; subsequent era years increment on the Gregorian New Year.
history: Era labels remain familiar in Japanese official forms and everyday records. They identify the chronology rather than a different month-length system.
example: 30 April 2019 was Heisei 31; 1 May 2019 was Reiwa 1. Gregorian 2026 is Reiwa 8.
limits: Before 1 January 1873 Japanese civil dates were lunisolar. The provider's Gregorian projections for Meiji years 1–5 are not original historical civil notation.
model: The provider uses the recorded modern imperial era boundaries and Gregorian month/day arithmetic, with the era-year number relative to the Gregorian starting year.
